evals.prompt: Our payment service has been experiencing intermittent 504 Gateway Timeouts for 48 hours during peak traffic. Symptoms: CPU is at 40%, memory is stable, DB connection pool is 85% utilized, Redis latency spiked twice, and only requests touching the fraud-check webhook fail. Some engineers blame Redis timeouts, others blame DB connection pool exhaustion, and others suspect third-party fraud webhook rate-limiting. Apply the Analysis of Competing Hypotheses (ACH) method to evaluate these root causes.
evals.expected_output: An ACH evaluation with an evidence matrix, consistency ratings (++ to --), focus on inconsistencies to eliminate hypotheses, sensitivity analysis, and the most diagnostic next probe.
assertions: Defines clear, mutually exclusive hypotheses for the incident
Includes an ACH comparison matrix mapping evidence items against each hypothesis with consistency symbols
Evaluates hypotheses by focusing on inconsistencies rather than merely tallying supporting points
Explicitly evaluates the diagnostic value of the fraud-check webhook failure
Identifies high-value diagnostic information gaps or tests to run next

evals.prompt: We detected an unexpected AWS IAM role assumption from an external IP at 02:00 UTC. The role belongs to our CI/CD runner. Hypotheses: (1) Compromised CI runner token, (2) Authorized developer debugging from home VPN, (3) Misconfigured third-party security scanner. Apply ACH to structure this investigation and avoid confirmation bias.
evals.expected_output: A structured ACH report contrasting evidence (IP reputation, CloudTrail event parameters, MFA usage, session duration) across all three hypotheses, identifying diagnostic differentiators.
assertions: Structures analysis across all three candidate hypotheses
Distinguishes between diagnostic evidence and neutral/non-diagnostic facts
Constructs a weighted or symbolic consistency matrix
Provides a sensitivity analysis and clear confidence assessment
